'''Barbara Anna Schaal''' (born 1947 in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], naturalized in 1956) is a [[Germany|German]]-born [[United States|American]] [[professor]], [[scientist]], and [[evolutionary biologist]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and served as vice president of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] from 2005 to 2013.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=McGinn |first=Susan Killenberg |date=2019-03-29 |title=Schaal to conclude Arts & Sciences deanship - The Source - Washington University in St. Louis |url=https://source.wustl.edu/2019/03/schaal-to-conclude-arts-sciences-deanship/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=The Source |language=en-US}}</ref> She is the first woman to be elected vice president of the academy.  From 2009 to 2017, Schaal served on the [[President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology]] (PCAST).<ref>{{cite web |title=Barbara A. Schaal |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/barbara-a-schaal-1bq14n/ |access-date=April 24, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=PCAST Members |url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/administration/eop/ostp/pcast/about/members |via=[[NARA|National Archives]] |work=[[Office of Science and Technology Policy]] |access-date=April 24, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Barbara A. Schaal {{!}} Chancellor search {{!}} Washington University in St. Louis |url=https://chancellorsearch.wustl.edu/barbara-a-schaal/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=chancellorsearch.wustl.edu}}</ref>

== Education ==
Schaal grew up in [[Chicago]], graduated from the [[University of Illinois, Chicago]] with a degree in [[biology]], and received a doctorate from [[Yale University]] in 1974.

== Area of expertise ==
Schaal is best known for her work on the [[genetics]] of plant species. She is known particularly well for her studies that use molecular genetic data to understand evolutionary processes such as [[gene flow]], geographical differentiation, and the [[domestication]] of crop species.<ref name="AAAS" />

== Career ==
Schaal was on the faculty of the [[University of Houston]] and [[Ohio State University]] before joining Washington University in 1980, where she has served as chair of the biology department. In 2009, Schaal was named the Mary-Dell Chilton Distinguished Professor in Arts & Sciences at Washington University.  She was formerly the director of [[Tyson Research Center]] and has been president of the [[Botanical Society of America]] and president of the [[Society for the Study of Evolution]].<ref name="AAAS" /><ref name="WUSTLnews" />

Schaal served as [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis|Washington University's dean of Arts & Sciences]] from January 1, 2013, through the 2019–20 academic year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nationally renowned professor named Dean of Arts and Sciences |date=4 October 2012 |publisher=Student Life |url=http://www.studlife.com/news/faculty-news/2012/10/04/nationally-renowned-professor-named-dean-of-arts-sciences/ |access-date=April 24, 2015}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2015 Schaal was elected as president of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and assumed the position in 2016.<ref name="WUSTLnews">{{cite web |title=Barbara Schaal chosen president-elect of AAAS |date=30 January 2015 |publisher=Washington University in St. Louis |url=http://news.wustl.edu/news/Pages/27966.aspx |access-date=April 24, 2015}}</ref><ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Barbara Schaal Chosen to Serve as AAAS President-Elect |publisher=AAAS |url=http://www.aaas.org/news/barbara-schaal-chosen-serve-aaas-president-elect |access-date=April 24, 2015}}</ref> In her president's address at AAAS' 2017 annual meeting, held Feb. 16–20 in Boston, titled 'Science and Technology for the Public Good,' she discussed the value of science and told the audience of scientists, students, journalists and science communicators that 'it is our obligation as scientists and citizens to speak up for science ... be a force for science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://publicnow.com/|title=Public {{!}} Your Web Disclosure Platform ·|website=publicnow.com|language=en|access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref>

Schaal established both the Distinguished Teaching Award and the Faculty Leadership Award in 2014 as a way to recognize exceptional commitment to Arts & Sciences and its students.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2017/10/arts-sciences-recognizes-faculty-excellence-teaching-leadership/|title=Arts & Sciences recognizes faculty for excellence in teaching, leadership {{!}} The Source {{!}} Washington University in St. Louis|date=2017-10-03|work=The Source|access-date=2018-02-03|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2023, Schaal was elected as a member of the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oral history interview with Barbara A. Schaal |url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/af5v4ke |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Science History Institute Digital Collections |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=June 2023 - Visualizing Women in Science |url=https://diglib-legacy.amphilsoc.org/womeninscience/2023/06/01/june-tip-of-the-iceberg.html |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=diglib-legacy.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
